name: Chrome-QUIC
description: Real captured Chromium (via Playwright automation) over QUIC/HTTP-3, across cloudflare-quic.com and quic.nginx.org. Transport values are exact, zero-variance constants confirmed across n=19 sessions (idle_timeout_ms=30000, initial_max_data=15728640, initial_max_streams_bidi=100). HTTP/3: qpack_max_table_capacity=65536, requires H3_DATAGRAM/MAX_FIELD_SECTION_SIZE/QPACK_BLOCKED_STREAMS. cipher_suites turned out identical between classes (both offer the same 3 standard TLS 1.3 suites) so not used as a constraint. supported_groups_any_of intentionally NOT set for Chrome: the discriminating group (0x001e) is aioquic's signature, not Chrome's -- Chrome's own distinguishing group (0x11ec) showed some inconsistency across sessions in earlier data and isn't used as a hard constraint here, kept as a documented open question rather than an assumption. pq_key_share_expected intentionally NOT set: PQ rollout appears to be a slower-moving, possibly server-controlled experiment state rather than a fixed per-session property. active_connection_id_limit intentionally omitted: never captured for Chrome.

name: aioquic-library-client
description: Real captured aioquic reference HTTP/3 client, across cloudflare-quic.com and quic.nginx.org. Transport values are exact, zero-variance constants confirmed across n=30 sessions (idle_timeout_ms=60000, initial_max_data=1048576, initial_max_streams_bidi=128, active_connection_id_limit=8). HTTP/3: qpack_max_table_capacity=4096, requires ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL/QPACK_BLOCKED_STREAMS. supported_groups_any_of=[0x001e] added: confirmed present in all 30/30 real aioquic sessions and 0/19 real Chrome sessions -- a clean, 100% discriminator in this dataset, closing the gap that previously left A1 (handshake-only spoofing) undetectable. pq_key_share_expected=false kept: consistent False across all samples, aioquic is a fixed unmodified reference codebase with no PQ support in this version.
